parts.visual:
Startup A spends 3 weeks building a new filter for photos on iOS. They launch it, and 1 million teenagers download it.
Startup B spends 7 years in a laboratory trying to build a quantum computer that works at room temperature. They haven't sold a single product yet.

The Two Worlds:
1. Consumer Apps: Low technical risk, extremely high market risk. The code is easy; the challenge is getting fickle human beings to actually use it.
2. Deep Tech: Extremely high technical risk, low market risk. The market for a working quantum computer is guaranteed (infinite demand). The risk is whether the laws of physics will actually allow the startup to build it.
parts.audio: Deep tech startups do not compete on marketing or viral growth. They compete on fundamental scientific breakthroughs. They are building the infrastructure of the future, not just another way to order pizza.

questions.question: A startup is trying to engineer a new type of bacteria that eats ocean plastic. This is a classic 'Deep Tech' company. Why is it so hard for them to raise money from traditional VCs?
options: The Timeline. Traditional VC funds operate on a 10-year cycle. They need companies to exit fast. A Deep Tech biology company might need 15 years just to get past the FDA trials before they make a single dollar of revenue. Most VCs cannot wait that long.
questions.correct_answer: The Timeline. Traditional VC funds operate on a 10-year cycle. They need companies to exit fast. A Deep Tech biology company might need 15 years just to get past the FDA trials before they make a single dollar of revenue. Most VCs cannot wait that long.
questions.explanation: Deep tech requires 'Patient Capital', which is very rare in Silicon Valley.

questions.question: Listen to the Deep Tech founder explaining their hiring strategy. Who are they recruiting?
questions.tts_text: We don't hire 'Full Stack Web Developers'. Our core team consists of four PhDs in Plasma Physics from MIT and two Aerospace Engineers who used to work at NASA. We are literally doing rocket science.
options: Extreme Specialization. Deep Tech companies are not building web apps. They are attempting to invent new science. Therefore, the founders and early employees are almost always top-tier academic researchers and scientists.
questions.correct_answer: Extreme Specialization. Deep Tech companies are not building web apps. They are attempting to invent new science. Therefore, the founders and early employees are almost always top-tier academic researchers and scientists.
questions.explanation: You cannot 'fake it till you make it' in quantum mechanics.

questions.question: What is the concept of 'Technical Risk' vs. 'Market Risk'?
options: Market Risk is 'Will people buy this?' (Consumer App). Technical Risk is 'Is it physically possible to build this?' (Deep Tech). If you cure cancer (Deep Tech), the Market Risk is zero; everyone will buy it. But the Technical Risk is astronomical.
questions.correct_answer: Market Risk is 'Will people buy this?' (Consumer App). Technical Risk is 'Is it physically possible to build this?' (Deep Tech). If you cure cancer (Deep Tech), the Market Risk is zero; everyone will buy it. But the Technical Risk is astronomical.
questions.explanation: Deep tech founders fight against the universe, not against competitors.

questions.question: Because traditional VCs are hesitant to fund 15-year research projects, where do Deep Tech startups often get their early funding?
options: Government Grants. Agencies like DARPA (USA) or Horizon Europe provide massive, non-dilutive capital to scientists to fund radical, high-risk research that the private sector is too scared to touch.
questions.correct_answer: Government Grants. Agencies like DARPA (USA) or Horizon Europe provide massive, non-dilutive capital to scientists to fund radical, high-risk research that the private sector is too scared to touch.
questions.explanation: The internet itself was a government-funded Deep Tech project.
